title: The German government asks its citizens to stop using Microsoft's web browser Internet Explorer to protect their own security.
text: Microsoft Corporation is an American multinational technology conglomerate headquartered in Redmond, Washington. The company became influential in the rise of personal computers through software like Windows and has since expanded into areas such as Internet services, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and video gaming among others.

title: A Nuremberg court issues an arrest warrant for former Argentine leader Jorge Rafael Videla, on suspicion of killing a German man.
text: General Jorge Rafael Videla was an Argentine general, politician and dictator who served as the president of Argentina from 1976 to 1981 during the National Reorganization Process. He came to power in a March 1976 coup d'état that deposed Isabel Perón.

title: 11–21 February – 60th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 60th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 11 to 21 February 2010, with Werner Herzog as president of the jury. The opening film of the festival was Chinese director Wang Quan'an's romantic drama Apart Together, in competition, while the closing film is Japanese director Yoji Yamada's About Her Brother, which was screened out of competition.

title: More than 10,000 anti-fascist protesters successfully block a planned neo-Nazi march in Dresden.
text: Neo-Nazism comprises all social, political, and militant ideologies and movements that have professed or idealized Nazism, whether in whole or in part, since the end of World War II in 1945. Neo-Nazi individuals and organizations employ their ideology to promote what they perceive as the racial or ethnic supremacy of their own group; to incite or engage in hatred or discrimination against demographic minorities (o…

title: Three car bombs hit the Egyptian, German and Iranian embassies in the centre of the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, in quick succession, killing at least 30 people.
text: This is a list of terrorist incidents in Iraq during 2010. Major attacks include a 1 February attack killing 54 in Baghdad, and a 10 May attack killed 45 at a fabrics factory in Hillah.

title: With the song "Satellite", Germany's Lena wins the Eurovision Song Contest 2010, the first German victory since 1982.
text: Lena Johanna Therese Meyer-Landrut, also known by the mononym Lena, is a German singer. She rose to fame after representing Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2010 in Oslo, winning the event with the song "Satellite".

title: Germany's TanDEM-X satellite, whose aim it is to create the most precise 3D map of Earth's surface, obtains its first images.
text: TanDEM-X is a German twin satellite mission using interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR). It is developed in a public-private partnership between the German Aerospace centre (DLR) and EADS Astrium (now Airbus Defence and Space).

title: Christian Wulff is elected President of Germany.
text: Christian Wilhelm Walter Wulffn ˈvɪlhɛlm ˈvaltɐ ˈvʊlf] ; born 19 June 1959) is a retired German politician and lawyer who served as President of Germany from 2010 to 2012. A member of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), he previously served as minister president of the state of Lower Saxony from 2003 to 2010.

title: In a referendum, voters in the German state of Bavaria vote to ban smoking at all pubs and restaurants.
text: The Federal Republic of Germany is a federation and consists of sixteen partly sovereign "states".

title: Spain defeats Germany 1–0 to win its semi-final and for its first time, along with Netherlands make the 2010 FIFA World Cup Final.
text: The final match of the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the 19th edition of FIFA's competition for national football teams, was played at Soccer City in Johannesburg, South Africa, on 11 July 2010. It was contested by the Netherlands and Spain, the first and only time two European teams contested a World Cup final held outside of Europe, as all other finals held outside of Europe featured a South American side.

title: 2010 FIFA World Cup: Germany defeats Uruguay 3–2 to finish third.
text: The 2010 FIFA World Cup was the 19th FIFA World Cup, the world championship for men's national football teams. It took place in South Africa from 11 June to 11 July 2010.

title: At least eight people are injured after a tornado strikes the German island of Duene in the North Sea.
text: Düne is one of two islands in the German Bight that form the Archipelago of Heligoland, the other being Heligoland proper.

title: A massive stampede at the 2010 Love Parade in Duisburg kills 20 people and injures dozens more people.
text: On 24 July 2010, a crowd disaster at the 2010 Love Parade electronic dance music festival in Duisburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, caused the deaths of 21 people from suffocation as attendees sought to escape a ramp leading to the festival area. The disaster injured 652 people.

title: Dutch rider Ellen van Dijk wins the 2010 Sparkassen Giro.
text: Eleonora Maria "Ellen" van Dijk vɑn ˈdɛik]; born 11 February 1987) is a Dutch former professional road racing cyclist, who last rode for UCI Women's WorldTeam Lidl–Trek. Besides road cycling she was also a track cyclist until 2012.

title: German HIV-positive pop singer Nadja Benaissa is found guilty of grievous bodily harm after transmitting HIV to a man who had unprotected sex with her without her telling him of her condition.
text: Human immunodeficiency viruses are two species of Lentivirus (a subgroup of retrovirus) that infect humans. Over time, they cause acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), a condition in which progressive failure of the immune system allows life-threatening opportunistic infections and cancers to thrive.

title: 21–26 September – photokina in Cologne
text: Photokina is a trade fair held in Europe for the photographic and imaging industries. It is the world's largest such trade fair.

title: Germany celebrates 20 years of unification.
text: The Unification of Germany was a process of building the first nation-state for Germans with federal features based on the concept of Lesser Germany (one without the Habsburgs' multi-ethnic Austria or its German-speaking part). It commenced on 18 August 1866 with the adoption of the North German Confederation Treaty establishing the North German Confederation, initially a military alliance de facto dominated by th…

title: The German government pays its last World War I reparations.
text: Following their defeat in World War I, the Central Powers agreed to pay war reparations to the Allied Powers. Each defeated power was required to make payments in either cash or kind.

title: Freck Langsam, German no-budget Gangster Comedy film is released.
text: Freck Langsam is a German no-budget Gangster Comedy film. Written by Jürgen Becker and directed by Michael Schu, the spoken language is Trierisch, a Moselle Franconian dialect of High German from the city of Trier, where the film is set.

title: German identity cards are issued in the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 format and contain RFID chips with personally identifiable information including a biometric Photo and, if desired, two fingerprints.
text: The German Identity Card is issued to German nationals by local registration offices in Germany and diplomatic missions abroad, while it is produced at the Bundesdruckerei in Berlin.

title: Demonstrations in Wendland near Gorleben against CASTOR-transport.
text: Lüchow-Dannenberg is a district in Lower Saxony, Germany, which is usually referred to as Hanoverian Wendland or Wendland. It is bounded by (from the west and clockwise) the districts of Uelzen and Lüneburg and the states of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (district of Ludwigslust-Parchim), Brandenburg (district of Prignitz), and Saxony-Anhalt (districts of Stendal and Altmarkkreis Salzwedel).

title: The German Meteorological Service, Deutsche Wetterdienst, says December was the coldest December month since 1969 in Germany.
text: The Deutscher Wetterdienst or DWD, is the German Meteorological Service, based in Offenbach am Main, Hesse, which monitors weather and meteorological conditions over Germany. DWD provides weather services for the general public and for nautical, aviation, hydrometeorological or agricultural purposes.

title: “I Will Love You Monday (365)” by Aura Dione
text: "I Will Love You Monday" is a song by Danish singer-songwriter Aura Dione from her debut album Columbine. It was released as her debut single in Europe on 10 November 2009 by Island Records, except Denmark, where the original version, "I Will Love You Monday", was released as her third single in August 2008.
listen: I Will Love You Monday (365) Aura Dione

title: “I Like” by Keri Hilson
text: "I Like" is a song by American singer Keri Hilson. It was written and produced by German musicians David Jost and Robin Grubert and recorded by Hilson for the soundtrack for the German film Zweiohrküken.

title: “Bad Romance” by 15 January
text: "Bad Romance" is a song by American singer-songwriter Lady Gaga from her third extended play, The Fame Monster (2009)—the reissue of her debut studio album, The Fame (2008). Following an unauthorized demo leak, Gaga premiered the final version of the song during Alexander McQueen's 2010 Paris Fashion Week show in October 2009.

title: “Tik Tok” by 29 January
text: "Tik Tok" is the debut solo single by American singer Kesha, who co-wrote the song with its producers Dr. Luke and Benny Blanco.

title: “Alors on danse” by 12 March
text: "Alors on danse" is a song by Belgian singer Stromae. It was released in September 2009 in Belgium and in February 2010 in the rest of Europe.

title: “Satellite” by Lena
text: "Satellite" is a song by German singer Lena Meyer-Landrut. It was written by American songwriter Julie Frost and Danish songwriter John Gordon and recorded by Meyer-Landrut for Unser Star für Oslo, the German pre-selection show for the Eurovision Song Contest 2010.

title: “Don't Believe” by Mehrzad Marashi
text: "Don't Believe" is a song by German singer Mehrzad Marashi, the winner of the seventh season of Deutschland sucht den Superstar, the German version of Pop Idol. Written and produced by DSDS jury member Dieter Bohlen, it reached the top of the charts in Austria, Germany, and Switzerland and was later included on his debut album New Life.

title: “Wavin' Flag” by K'naan
text: "Wavin' Flag" is a song by Somali-Canadian artist K'naan from his album Troubadour. The song was originally written for Somalia and aspirations of its people for freedom.

title: “Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)” by Shakira featuring Freshlyground
text: "Waka Waka" is a song by Colombian singer Shakira, featuring the South African band Freshlyground. Co-written by Shakira and John Hill, it was released on 7 May 2010 by Epic Records as the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup, which was held in South Africa.
listen: Waka Waka (This Time for Africa) Shakira featuring Freshlyground

title: “We No Speak Americano” by 6 August
text: "We No Speak Americano" is a song by Australian band Yolanda Be Cool and producer DCUP. It was released on the independent Australian label Sweat It Out on 27 February 2010. The song samples the 1956 Italian song "Tu vuò fà l'americano" in the Neapolitan language by Renato Carosone, written by Carosone and Nicola Salerno.

title: “Love the Way You Lie” by Eminem featuring Rihanna
text: "Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery. Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid.
listen: Love the Way You Lie Eminem featuring Rihanna

title: “Somewhere Over the Rainbow/What a Wonderful World” by Israel "IZ" Kamakawiwoʻole
text: "Somewhere Over the Rainbow/What a Wonderful World" is a medley of "Over the Rainbow" by Judy Garland and "What a Wonderful World" by Louis Armstrong, recorded by Hawaiian singer Israel Kamakawiwoʻole. First released on the 1990 album Ka ʻAnoʻi, an acoustic rendition of the medley became notable after its release on his 1993 album Facing Future.

title: “We Are the People” by Empire of the Sun
text: "We Are the People" is a song by Australian electronic music duo Empire of the Sun, released as the second single from their debut studio album, Walking on a Dream. It was released in Australia on 20 September 2008 and debuted at number 85 on the ARIA Singles Chart before peaking at number 24 on 12 January 2009.
